title: The Number That Decided It
subtitle: YouTube · 16:9 · 0:24 — numbers carried four different ways, each decided by its sentence

nodes.label: Growth was not the number that decided the business
nodes.visual: Shot in the shop before opening, one light on. The evidence is the same room at four in the morning, not a dashboard.
nodes.summary: Four numbers appear in twenty-four seconds and none of them is drawn the same way. That is the point of the board: the sentence decides the carrier.

nodes.label: Forty loaves. That was a whole week.
nodes.visual: The figure itself, held: 40 set large on the shutter, nothing else in frame. No counter, no bar.
nodes.summary: A single quantity with nothing to compare it to yet. Drawing a chart here would invent a relationship the sentence does not have; the number is the image.

nodes.label: Forty loaves a week — stated, not compared
nodes.visual: 40 in heavy type on the closed shutter, slowly going out of focus as the shutter lifts. The figure is the subject; the frame does the animating.
nodes.summary: Carrier: type. The line states a figure, it does not compare one. This is the case where a chart would be a costume.

nodes.label: Forty to four hundred in eight months
nodes.visual: One line, drawn left to right, no gridlines, the two endpoints labelled directly. The line arrives with the word 'four hundred'.
nodes.summary: Carrier: chart. The sentence is about the move, not the bakery — there is no object in this script that can show a rise, so a line is the honest answer.

chart.what: one line, 40 to 400 over eight months, endpoints labelled
chart.why: the line is about the change in quantity over a period, and the script names both endpoints and the interval

nodes.label: Opened at four, every day, for thirty days
nodes.visual: The shop shutter going up, filmed thirty mornings, cut as a fast lift with one frame of darkness between. The count is carried by the repetition, not by dots.
nodes.summary: Carrier: object. Same script as the sales line, different answer — because this sentence is about a repeated action in a real place, and the footage already exists.
nodes.form: the shutter going up, thirty mornings, one frame each

nodes.label: One in ten came back a third time
nodes.visual: Ten tickets laid flat; one turned over to show a third stamp. If the tickets cannot be sourced, ten identical marks with one alive — the only schematic in the edit, and it is earned.
nodes.summary: Carrier: chart, with an object fallback. The sentence is literally a share of a whole, so a proportion is not decoration — it is the claim. The other nine stay visible; cropping them would lie.

chart.what: one of ten, the remainder kept visible
chart.why: the sentence states a share of a whole group, which is a relationship, and the whole is small enough to show completely

nodes.label: Count the number that decides whether they come back
nodes.visual: Back to the shop in daylight, one person at the counter. No graphic. The last frame has no number in it at all.
nodes.summary: The closing beat drops every carrier on purpose: after four numbers, the argument is carried by a person.

nodes.label: Four numbers, four different carriers — consistency comes from type and light, not from the graphics
nodes.summary: Different carriers are only coherent if the frame stays the same: same light, same shutter, same type face. If the four numbers look like four different videos, the carrier decision is not the problem — the visual system is.
